voices.note: the mishnah's list of disqualified officiants (15b), cited here by its lemma אונן
ואידך -- the anonymous author of the ומן המקדש derivation at 16a.14
דבי רבי ישמעאל תנא -- author of the baal-mum kal vachomer and its tzad-hashaveh repair

props.gloss_en: an (ordinary) priest in acute mourning who performed the service has desecrated it -- the mishnah's law under derivation
the anonymous derivation: the verse exempts only the High Priest from leaving; by inference any OTHER priest who did not leave (and served as onen) desecrated
R' Elazar's derivation: Aaron's 'I offered' implies that had his onen sons offered, the offering would rightly have been burned -- an onen's service disqualifies
the sin-offering of that day was burned because it became impure (so הן הקריבו proves nothing about aninut)
the sin-offering was burned because Aaron and his sons were acute mourners -- the reading הן הקריבו requires, held by R' Elazar and by the tanna of the kal vachomer
the ordinary priest is WARNED against serving as onen -- the premise the tzad hashaveh's common element needs

the fallback: even if the shem-yoshev pircha does refute, the law is derived from the seated scholar together with ANY ONE of those three (zar / tamei / baal mum) -- a conditional derivation with a disjunctive second source; no schema construct can state either feature, so it is recorded here as a proposition

schemas.gloss_en: if the blemished priest, who MAY EAT of offerings, desecrates the service if he served, then the onen, who may not eat, all the more so desecrates if he served

grounds.gloss_en: מה לבעל מום שכן עשה בו קריבין כמקריבין -- with blemishes the Torah equated disqualified ANIMALS with disqualified officiants, a stringency aninut lacks

answered_by.gloss_en: זר יוכיח -- the non-priest has no sacrifice-equals-officiant stringency, yet his service desecrates

schemas.gloss_en: לא ראי זה כראי זה: the common element of the blemished priest and the non-priest -- they are warned off the service, and if they served they desecrated -- brings in the onen, who is warned

grounds.gloss_en: מה להצד השוה שבהן שכן לא הותרה מכללו -- neither source's prohibition is EVER permitted, whereas aninut is permitted from its rule for the High Priest

answered_by.gloss_en: טמא יוכיח -- impurity IS permitted from its rule (for communal offerings), yet the impure priest desecrates

schemas.gloss_en: הצד השוה שבהן שמוזהרין ואם עבדו חיללו -- the common element of the impure, the blemished and the non-priest brings in the onen

grounds.gloss_en: ולפרוך: מה להצד השוה שבהן שכן לא הותרו מכללן אצל כהן גדול בקרבן יחיד -- none of the three is permitted even to a High Priest for an individual offering, whereas the onen High Priest serves even individual offerings

answered_by.gloss_en: שם טומאה מיהא אישתראי -- the CATEGORY of impurity is at least permitted (for communal offerings), so the three do not share the claimed no-exception stringency; the objection is deflected and the schema stands

schemas.gloss_en: if the seated priest, who may eat of offerings, desecrates the service if he served seated, then the onen, who may not eat, all the more so

grounds.gloss_en: מה ליושב שכן פסול לעדות -- one who sits is disqualified from testifying, a stringency the onen lacks

answered_by.gloss_en: מיושב תלמיד חכם -- derive instead from the seated Torah scholar, who IS fit to testify seated, yet desecrates the service if he served seated

objections.gloss_en: ורבי אלעזר מאי טעמא לא אמר מומן המקדש לא יצא -- why prefer הן הקריבו over the explicit chillul verse?

answered_by.gloss_en: מי כתיב הא אחר שלא יצא חילל?! -- the ordinary-priest clause is only an inference, never written; it is not conclusive

objections.gloss_en: ואידך מאי טעמא לא אמר מהן הקריבו -- why does the anonymous derivation shun R' Elazar's source?

answered_by.gloss_en: קסבר מפני טומאה נשרפה -- on his reading the sin-offering was burned for impurity, so הן הקריבו carries no aninut law

objections.gloss_en: היכן מוזהר? אילימא מומן המקדש לא יצא -- חילול בגופיה כתיב ביה! -- if the warning is that verse, desecration is written outright and the kal vachomer is unnecessary

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא מהן הקריבו -- וקסבר מפני אנינות נשרפה: the warning premise rides on R' Elazar's source, read as an aninut consequence
